maya: FYI — noticed a sharp p99/p99.9 tail increase on the attn-optim kernels during the canary run this morning. baseline -> canary: p99 +18ms, p99.9 +42ms. no large change in median.
liam: ugh. is this on real traffic or synthetic harness?
sasha: synthetic harness (v3) with heavy short-seq mix (avg 32). i re-ran with the real-traffic trace and saw a much smaller delta (~+4ms p99).
ciara: could this be an interaction with batching or continuous batching heuristics? short sequences change batching profile.
maya: stack: kernel-selector@0.9.1 + attn-opt kernels from forked branch. harness: bench-runner v3 (we switched sampling window to 60s last week).
liam: two hypotheses: 1) selector chooses a different kernel for short sequences that has worse tail when under bursty arrivals, 2) measurement artifact from the shorter sample window. we should reproduce with controlled Poisson arrivals.
sasha: reproduced with trace-replay + poisson overlay. when arrival burstiness increases, that kernel's p99 blows up. median fine. seems queuing related.
ciara: can you paste the repro command?
sasha: ```
# replay recorded trace with poisson overlay
perf-replay --trace traces/2026-03-06-shortseq.json --overlay poisson --rate 120 --duration 300 
perf-collect --percentiles 50,95,99,99.9 --window 60 --out out.json
```
liam: also run with `--seq-dist real` vs `--seq-dist synthetic` so kernel selector sees the same distribution as production. selector uses seq-dist histogram to pick kernel.
benchbot: bench-runner job #7845 finished. commit: 7f3a2d9. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/7f3a2d9/7845/out.json
maya: important note — the canary also used driver nv-530. driver roll happened on the canary nodes last week. unknown if related.
ciara: add driver version to perf logs and enable `kernel-fallback` logs. if it's a driver-induced jitter that would explain tail only.
liam: for methodology we need to standardize: 1) fixed arrival pattern (poisson + recorded spikes), 2) compare both seq-dist-aware selector and a pinned-kernel baseline, 3) run 10 independent trials, 4) report mean + bootstrap CI for percentiles.
sasha: agreed. also include per-request token-count and queue-time histograms so we can separate queueing vs kernel exec time.
maya: quick correctness check: run golden-eval on 200 prompts and ensure logprob diffs < 1e-5 and deterministic outputs for CPU path. i saw one sample with token mismatch earlier (likely due to quant path).
ciara: i've sketched a triage checklist: reproduce -> isolate (pin kernel/driver) -> collect per-component latencies -> run bootstrap significance -> decide revert vs mitigation. i'll attach to the ticket. :white_check_mark:
liam: mitigation options if we confirm regression: A) force selector to prefer older kernel for short sequences, B) temporarily set `kernel-fallback=enabled` (slower median but stable tail), C) pin node driver to nv-520.
maya: can someone run the 10-trial bootstrap by EOD? I'll try the driver-pin test locally.
sasha: i'll own the pinned-kernel baseline runs. starting now. posting artifacts to thread when done.
benchbot: perf-run started: job 7851 (pinned-kernel baseline). monitoring.
ciara: also add a tiny synthetic test to CI that replays a 30s burst trace and asserts p99 < 120ms. we can make it flaky-tolerant with retries but it'll catch regressions early.
liam: good call. we must avoid brittle percentiles in CI; use bootstrap + tolerances.
maya: action items: @sasha baseline runs, @ciara add CI synthetic burst test + ticket, @liam add doc PR describing the standardized methodology and the bootstrap script, @maya try driver pin and report.
deploy-bot: scheduled patch release (candidate) will include `kernel-fallback` flag and additional logging: release/candidate-2026-03-06-kerntailfix -> canary tonight 22:00 UTC.
liam: thanks everyone — if baseline shows kernel is the culprit we'll pin selector until we have a perf-validated replacement.
maya: thanks, will update thread with artifacts and a short table of percentile deltas. :rocket:
